entry.title: [Soroushdabbagh_Official] Thanks to a dear friend living in Europe, I recently received images of the…
entry.summary:
Source: @Soroushdabbagh_Official

Thanks to a dear friend living in Europe, I recently received images of the paper copies of my three recent books, "In the Struggle of Suffering and Meaning," "In the Passage of Time: A Stroll in the Garden of Bu Sa'id," and "Velvet Whispers: Existential Murmurs," which have been published over the past three years. Looking at these images and then reviewing the table of contents of the aforementioned trilogy, the many hours, days, and weeks spent on contemplation, research, and writing them paraded before my eyes and blew a pleasant feeling toward me. Among the essays included in these books, I personally prefer "Dostoevsky; the Modern Pilgrim of Thoughtful Suffering," "The Modern Pilgrim, Touching Presence, and Experiencing Boredom," and "From Correspondence Truth to Persuasive-Narrative Truth"; which not only contain the author's fresh ideas but also, in the process of writing and finalizing them, I savored "flow" as narrated by Csikszentmihalyi to the extent of my ability. A flow that is a blend of challenge, knowledge, and skill and requires spending a great deal of time; a flow that is of the kind of mental and psychological sweating... On the other hand, I deeply love the book "Velvet Whispers," which is of the essence of Soroush Dabbagh and is deeply intertwined with his existence and existential concerns, depicting his very self... These days, alongside my work engagements and commitments, I am writing the introduction to the book "Narratives of Suffering and War." Thanks to the efforts of the editor and the esteemed publisher, the book is on the verge of being finalized. I hope my last spiritual child, which "like a basket full of fruit has a high fever of ripening," will be finalized by the end of Shahrivar and be placed before the eyes of those interested.... https://www.instagram.com/p/Dc1qf6HqAAk/?igsi=MXM0YXAwMW16c3RhZg==

entry.title: [Soroushdabbagh_Official] At his suggestion, I read the book "The History of God" with pleasure and…
entry.summary:
Source: @Soroushdabbagh_Official

At his suggestion, I read the book "The History of God" with pleasure and benefited from it. During the time I was translating Wittgenstein's Tractatus and writing a commentary on it, I consulted with Mr. Salki about some of the equivalents I was choosing and benefited from his considerations. I remember that after the presidential election of 2009 (1388) and the uproar it had stirred up, one day he said to me out of kindness and affection: "My friend, do you know how much respect I have for your scientific and cultural standing, your father's, and the works you have published? I wish you had not gotten involved in politics, or that politics had not gotten involved with you, and that you had only devoted yourself to scholarly and cultural work!" While thanking him, I said that dealing with politics is one of the exigencies of intellectual work and religious reformism in the Middle East and in a country like Iran. I remember hearing similar kind words from the late Dr. Karim Mojtahedi after I finished my lecture at the two-day seminar on "Islamic Philosophy" held in the second half of the 2000s (1380s) at the Iranian Institute of Philosophy... Yesterday, I was saddened by the news of the passing of Dr. Behzad Salki, and many pleasant memories of him from the time I resided at the "Iranian Institute of Philosophy" came alive in my mind and heart. Alas, our meeting was postponed until the Day of Resurrection, and after leaving Iran in the late 2000s (1380s), I never found the opportunity to converse and sit with this dear departed one. I pray with all my heart for patience upon this tragedy for his respected family, relatives, and friends. May his soul be happy! : Since you have commanded me to pray, O wonder! Make this prayer of mine answered

entry.title: [Soroushdabbagh_Official] "This caravan of life passes wondrously." Twenty years ago, after completing my…
entry.summary:
Source: @Soroushdabbagh_Official

"This caravan of life passes wondrously." Twenty years ago, after completing my philosophical studies at the University of Warwick in England, I returned to Tehran and, as a faculty member and assistant professor, began teaching and researching at the "Iranian Institute of Philosophy." During that five-year period, my office was near Dr. Behzad Salki's office. For this reason, on average, we saw each other twice a week; either he would come to my office, or I would go to his, and we would drink tea and talk together. I remember that in our first meetings, we discussed the book "Philosophy of Religion" by John Hick, which had been translated by him and published under the name Behzad Rad. In the 1990s (1370s), when I was a pharmacy student, a few friends interested in philosophical topics and I would read different chapters of Hick's translated book weekly and discuss them. Later, in the 2000s (1380s), we discussed John Hick's "The Fifth Dimension," which had been translated into Persian by Behzad Salki, with several philosophy-researching friends. At that time, I did not know that the translator of both books was the same person, and that Behzad Rad was the pen name of Mr. Behzad Salki. When I mentioned this to Behzad Salki, he laughed and said: "I preferred that at that time, Hick's works, which had just come before the eyes of Persian-speaking philosophy researchers, not be published under my name, because 'the passage of well-being was narrow.'" Dr. Salki was a pleasant, humble, and sincere person, and a tranquility emanated from him. He had nothing to do with anger, jealousy, or harshness, and he enjoyed great mental health. I do not recall him speaking ill of anyone. In our conversations, we talked about the books we were reading and our work and research projects. He was aware of my great fondness for Sepehri and Wittgenstein, and out of kindness, he introduced me to some good Persian and English works in these areas, most of which I read with enthusiasm. He had a close friendship with the esteemed professor Baha' al-Din Khorramshahi. He had interesting memories about the process of translating the book "A History of God" by Karen Armstrong, which had been translated into Persian by Khorramshahi and him, and I delighted in hearing them....👇👇👇 https://www.instagram.com/p/Dcwpaucx867/?igsi=N3k3MHY5bmliZjRn

entry.title: [Soroushdabbagh_Official] Last week, to find an answer to the question posed by the esteemed website…
entry.summary:
Source: @Soroushdabbagh_Official

Last week, to find an answer to the question posed by the esteemed website "Sedanat" about the names of Iranian and non-Iranian thinkers and intellectuals (including philosophers, psychologists, poets, novelists, etc.) who, over the past few decades, have played a role in shaping and consolidating my intellectual and written work, and from whom I have received tangible and palpable influences, I retreated to a corner. I rode on the wings of memories and, to the best of my ability, delved into the labyrinthine fortress of memory, the readings, writings, and lived experiences of the past thirty-five years. It was a nostalgic and soul-nourishing journey. The outcome of this inner journey, which started on its own and arrived at its own conclusion, was as follows: names with whose works, teachings, intellectual sparks, and existential embers I have been intimately familiar and conversant for many years, breathing in their atmosphere. A long-standing companionship and association that has also spilled into my essays, books, and lectures: Abu al-Hasan Kharaqani, Abu Sa'id Abi al-Khayr, Sheikh Shahab al-Din Suhrawardi, Saadi, Rumi, Shams Tabrizi, Hafez of Shiraz, Kant, Kierkegaard, Dostoevsky, Tolstoy, Jung, Kazantzakis, David Ross, Wittgenstein, Heidegger, Forough Farrokhzad, Abraham Maslow, Albert Camus, Erich Fromm, Ali Shariati, Sohrab Sepehri, Akhavan Sales, Abdolhossein Zarrinkoub, Shamlou, Isaiah Berlin, Gadamer, John Hick, Simin Daneshvar, Dariush Shayegan, Dariush Ashouri, Abdolkarim Soroush, Mojtahed Shabestari, Mostafa Malekian, and Irvin Yalom. https://www.instagram.com/p/DcrMtPfqnIv/?igsi=MzZhZTJiZW9kaXZj

entry.title: [Soroushdabbagh_Official] "Happy were the times spent with a friend." These days I am traveling in…
entry.summary:
Source: @Soroushdabbagh_Official

"Happy were the times spent with a friend." These days I am traveling in Europe. Yesterday, I found the opportunity to sit with Mohammad Rahbar at one of the Iranian coffee shops in London, where the scent of Hafez and the city of Shiraz wafts through the air, and we talked for a few hours. It was a valuable meeting; about politics, literature, poetry, reading, and writing... we spoke and listened. Dear Mohammad, in the early days of the forty-day war, he showed admirable courage and integrity by leaving the "Iran International" media outlet; a media outlet that, at least during the twelve-day war and the forty-day war, sadly mixed oil and water, engaged in lies and fabrication, and played a significant role in constructing and reinforcing a narrative that sought to normalize war, as I mentioned in the essay "War, Narrative-Building, and Political Blockage," leaving behind a bitter and shocking anti-patriotic record. Moreover, some Persian-speaking employees of this outlet, during the days when the slingshot of fate rained stones of sedition and missiles rained from the sky onto their compatriots inside the country, leaving them wounded and dead, sat opposite a prime minister who has been called a war criminal by international courts, and with smiles on their lips and body language that reeked of satisfaction and joy, interviewed the main person responsible for the aggression against their country's land and waters, and their disgrace fell from the rooftop for all to see. If I were in the place of those who set about justifying the crime at the Minab school and whitewashing the blatant aggression of Israel and America against their country's soil over the past year, who broke all the pots over the Islamic Republic's head and did not say a harsher word to the enemy of their land and water than a delicate flower, I would melt with embarrassment and feel ashamed. Not to mention that some of these same media figures, using the pure blood of dear young people who were sadly and unjustly spilled on the ground in January of last year as a pretext, made mountains out of molehills without any basis or sufficient evidence, and in their videos fed blatant lies to the helpless, desperate, and oppressed people, earning more audience and making money for themselves: it is fitting that blood surges in the heart of the ruby-colored mourning, for shards are breaking the market of the potter. I am glad that dear Mohammad, despite all the insults and accusations he heard, despite all the arrows of blame fired at him by former colleagues, was not intimidated by the atmosphere; he held his head high, steeled his resolve, and left this organization and media outlet, which, whatever it is, is not national-patriotic, and came to a good end: Two things are the fruit of life: a good name and reward; if you pass beyond these two, all that is on it shall perish. https://www.instagram.com/p/DcoIobjMo54/?igsi=dnp6MzVzajY0djFj

entry.summary:
Source: @Soroushdabbagh_Official

Dear Dr. Gerami, with greetings and respect. I hope you are well and healthy. I am a final-semester engineering student, about to enter the humanities at the master's level. For some time now, a question has been forming in my mind, the answer to which I have not found in texts, lectures, or lessons; for it is not a question of "what to read" or "how to write," but of "how to be." My concern is not the research method, but the researcher's character. More precisely, I want to know what qualities a humanities graduate must cultivate in themselves so that on the last day they are not merely a book-learned specialist, but a human being living in the deep and precise sense of the word. Does academic life, combined with pain and concern, require a "special character"? What kind of being is being a humanities student? Can this being be acquired through practice? Or is the answer fundamentally personal, and each person's path is unique to them? If possible, please guide me on this path from your perspective and lived experience. With infinite gratitude for the time you spend and renewed respect. 👇👇👇

entry.title: [Soroushdabbagh_Official] An excerpt from the article "In the Spirit of Ludwig and Sohrab" by Soroush…
entry.summary:
Source: @Soroushdabbagh_Official

An excerpt from the article "In the Spirit of Ludwig and Sohrab" by Soroush Dabbagh, in which he refers to a verse by Bidel Dehlavi: "Hope always pertains to the future. A person who lives in the present is neither hopeful nor hopeless. As Bidel Dehlavi, who had a significant influence on Sohrab Sepehri's poetry and thought, put it: In this gathering, hope and despair each have their own intoxication—I am glad that they made me drunk with the pain of being without quality. Whether one is hopeful or hopeless, each carries its own intoxication or trouble. The poet is content that he has fallen into a state of being without quality or without hope. Along the same lines, Wittgenstein emphasizes indifference toward the surrounding world. This attitude highlights not being dependent on external events and their misfortunes." https://t.me/Biddle_Academy

entry.title: [Soroushdabbagh_Official] .«Life is not something that slips from the memory of me and you off the ledge…
entry.summary:
Source: @Soroushdabbagh_Official

.«Life is not something that slips from the memory of me and you off the ledge of habit/Life is the whistle of a train that turns a corner in a dream.» Over the past five years, we have held 10 rounds of 10-session group therapy sessions together with dear Dr. Hossein Sani: 2 rounds on "Death Anxiety," 1 advanced round on "Death Anxiety," 3 rounds on "The Meaning of Life," 3 rounds on "Loneliness," and one 15-session round "with an existential approach." In addition, we completed a one-year, fifty-session "group therapy" course together with dear clients and fellow travelers; a long and instructive existential journey that was a valuable and soul-soothing experience for every fellow traveler. A few months ago, I reread the readable book "The Schopenhauer Cure" by Irvin Yalom, translated into Persian by Sepideh Habib. It was a delightful experience and brought to life in my mind and heart many of the dialogues and atmospheres of the group therapy sessions held over the past five years. "For a while, this Masnavi was delayed." After nearly a two-year hiatus, we plan to start a new 15-session "group psychotherapy with an existential approach" course together with dear Dr. Sani from mid-October (around mid-Mehr month), with sessions held on Saturdays at 11 AM North American time, virtually. Friends interested in participating in this group therapy course, given the limited capacity, please message as soon as possible for information and registration at number 4167350042 (code 001) on WhatsApp or on the Instagram page soroush_dabbagh. The therapist-client relationship is like that of two fellow travelers who begin the journey from a specific point and move forward together, but do not know in advance where and at which point the journey will end, for "no one knows what the outcome will be." In my psychotherapy practice over the past nearly six years, I have many times begun, advanced, and completed therapeutic journeys together with clients; experiences that have been instructive and enjoyable in their own right and have greatly aided my self-awareness, self-exploration, and self-knowledge. The healing process occurs beautifully in a group; when trust is established and you share your concerns, preoccupations, and lived experiences with group members and therapists without fear or worry of being judged, and you taste and savor being understood. Moreover, on this long therapeutic journey, you become familiar with the experiences and life-worlds of other group members and look at the world through their windows as well.. https://www.instagram.com/p/DcZuXVQM8e4/?igsi=MTduMjEzeHVobjk2Zg==
